query: Starting from an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state and a target density below 6 g/cm3, what single intervention could overcome performance limitations associated with stable intermetallic formation while improving room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts measurable changes relative to the as-processed baseline, defines the relevant composition, temperature, exposure-time, and test-environment boundaries, cites supporting evidence from previously reported Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys, and proposes a controlled experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of a small amount of Nb (e.g., 0.2%) to the Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy can overcome performance limitations associated with stable intermetallic formation while improving room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation.
generation.material_initial_state: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state
generation.intervention: Addition of a small amount of Nb (e.g., 0.2%)
generation.conditions: Target density below 6 g/cm3, room temperature, and high-temperature oxidation environment
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a BCC solid solution and segregation of Nb into the interdendritic region
generation.mechanism: The addition of Nb enhances the corrosion resistance and high-temperature oxidation resistance by forming a protective film on the surface of the alloy, and improves the room-temperature compressive behavior by strengthening the alloy through solid solution hardening
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation
generation.boundary: Target density below 6 g/cm3, room temperature, and high-temperature oxidation environment
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Nb required to achieve the desired properties, and the potential effects of other alloying elements on the properties of the alloy

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys, one with the addition of 0.2% Nb and one without, and test their room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation
measurements: Corrosion rate in a 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution
Weight gain after high-temperature oxidation at 1000 °C for 50 h
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy with the addition of 0.2% Nb does not show improved room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation compared to the alloy without Nb, then the hypothesis is falsified
